records.title: Ballistic test results for several different soft body armor systems
records.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
license_notes: The Data.gov record explicitly points to the NIST data licence.

NIST employee-created non-standard-reference data are generally not subject to US copyright under 17 U.S.C. 105; NIST's licence also addresses possible foreign copyright and grants rights subject to its terms.
Retain NIST attribution and the as-is/no-warranty notice.
Any modified data must carry a notice identifying the modification date and nature.

source_standard_context.warning: This dataset predates NIJ 0101.07 and does not establish conformity to NIJ 0101.07 or NIJ 0123.00.

declared_contents.panel_identity: not declared in catalog metadata; must be checked against archive README and CSV contents before attempting panel-wise validation

associated_method_reference.title: Analysis of Three Different Regression Models to Estimate the Ballistic Performance of New and Environmentally Conditioned Body Armor
associated_method_reference.panel_validation_method: leave-one-panel-out cross-validation: fit on n-1 panels, test on the held-out panel, repeat for each panel (NISTIR 7760 section 3.1.5)

intended_benchmark_use: historical reproduction of the NISTIR 7760 statistical analysis
known_limitations: Only six armour-system CSV files are declared.
The CSV schema contains velocity and binary perforation outcome; it does not provide material/process descriptors suitable for architecture-level transfer claims.
The data are historical and tied to the NIJ 0101.06 context.
The source is not an NIJ Compliant Products List and the dataset is not a product conformity assessment.

Catalog metadata declares velocity and binary perforation outcome columns but does not establish that panel identity is retained in the downloadable CSVs; panel-wise cross-validation may therefore be impossible from the released archive.
